The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they’re already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.
The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_
The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.
Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a
SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.
The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages
should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page
The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added
pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly
The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login
pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and

the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar

The Landing Page should be a simple page with the Navigation Bar and Profile Icon
and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use
the database to retrieve the user’s name and include it in the welcome message to
make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that
function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar
The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with
dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The
dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team
should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here
(Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should
include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns
The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information
about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the
actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This
should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log
The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their
own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the
page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone
number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally).
The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or
Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request
